run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-17T11:08:03Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The frontend error signal that opened this investigation is explained by the product-catalog Deployment in namespace otel-demo having its container command set to ["invalid-command"]. A new ReplicaSet (product-catalog-fcf7564cf, created 2026-11-17T11:06:12Z, same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog as the previous ReplicaSet product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc) carries that command; its pods fail at container init with exitCode 128 / reason StartError ('exec: "invalid-command": executable file not found in $PATH') and the surviving pod product-catalog-fcf7564cf-vjj7l is Ready=False in CrashLoopBackOff with 5 restarts. The Deployment's Service product-catalog has zero ready endpoint addresses (only notReadyAddresses 100.96.2.148). The previous product-catalog pod was killed at 11:06:21Z, and frontend's cumulative STATUS_CODE_ERROR span counter was flat at 2045 until 11:07:15Z before climbing to 15534 by 11:17:30Z; in 11:05:00-11:17:35 frontend produced about 13347 error spans versus 0 new error spans in the 10:17:35-11:05:00 baseline. frontend's error spans are concentrated on grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct (2451.2) and GET /api/products/{productId} (2451.2), plus GetProduct-dependent paths (recommendation 468.3, checkout 327.1). recommendation (944 error spans, on its ProductCatalogService/ListProducts client call) and checkout (584.5 error spans, on its ProductCatalogService/GetProduct client call) show their own error spans on the same dependency, and frontend-proxy shows 7243.9 ingress/router-egress error spans in the incident window versus 7.15 in the baseline. cart, currency, shipping, payment, accounting and fraud-detection showed no error-span increase; ad's error count was unchanged from background. The specific actor or mechanism that changed the Deployment pod template (generation 4) could not be determined because change history is not integrated, and the alert's own expression could not be verified because no alerting rules and no http_server_request_duration_seconds_count series exist in this Prometheus; those are recorded as gaps.

claims.text: Deployment product-catalog in namespace otel-demo (generation 4, spec.replicas 1) has container command ["invalid-command"] with image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog, and its status reports no available or ready replicas.

Two ReplicaSets exist for Deployment product-catalog: product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc (created 2026-11-17T10:36:11Z, replicas 0, no command override, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog) and product-catalog-fcf7564cf (created 2026-11-17T11:06:12Z, replicas 1, command ["invalid-command"], same image), so the pod template was changed at about 11:06:12Z with the image unchanged.

Pod product-catalog-fcf7564cf-vjj7l is phase Running but Ready=False (ContainersNotReady) with restartCount 5, container state waiting reason CrashLoopBackOff, and lastState terminated with exitCode 128, reason StartError and message 'failed to create containerd task: ... exec: "invalid-command": executable file not found in $PATH'.

Events in otel-demo record the failure sequence: ReplicaSet product-catalog-fcf7564cf SuccessfulCreate of pod product-catalog-fcf7564cf-2fvnx at 11:06:12Z; that pod Failed at 11:06:17Z with 'exec: "invalid-command": executable file not found in $PATH' and BackOff at 11:06:17Z; pod product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-wzpwm Killing at 11:06:21Z with Deployment 'Scaled down replica set product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc from 1 to 0'; Deployment 'Scaled up replica set product-catalog-fcf7564cf from 0 to 1' at 11:06:29Z; pod product-catalog-fcf7564cf-vjj7l Failed at 11:09:42Z with the same invalid-command message and BackOff at 11:11:44Z.

The Service product-catalog (selector opentelemetry.io/name=product-catalog, port 8080) currently has zero ready endpoint addresses and one notReadyAddress 100.96.2.148 belonging to pod product-catalog-fcf7564cf-vjj7l.

product-catalog span activity decayed to 0: its rate was about 13 spans/s through roughly 11:08Z, 3.21/s at 11:10:35Z and 0 from 11:12:35Z onward, consistent with the pod ceasing to serve after the 11:06Z replacement.

frontend's cumulative STATUS_CODE_ERROR span counter stayed flat at 2045 from 11:00:00Z through 11:07:15Z, rose to 3482 at 11:07:30Z, and reached 15534 by 11:17:30Z; a 5-minute-window increase series is 0 at every step from 10:48Z through 11:06:40Z and rises from 516.67 at 11:07:40Z to a peak of 7043.03 at 11:16:40Z.

frontend produced about 13346.8 error spans in 11:05:00-11:17:35 versus 0 in the 10:17:35-11:05:00 baseline; within the incident window its error spans are GET 3261.8, GET /api/products/{productId} 2451.2, grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct 2451.2, GET /api/recommendations 468.3, grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations 468.3, POST /api/checkout and POST 327.1, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 327.1, and tcp.connect 18.1, while GET/POST /api/cart and CartService client spans stayed at 0 (these are span counts, not request counts).

recommendation's own error spans rose from 2.04 in the 10:17:35-11:05:00 baseline to about 944.0 in 11:05:00-11:17:35, located on its client call /oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/ListProducts (471.5) and internal span get_product_list (471.5).

checkout appears with 584.5 error spans in 11:05:00-11:17:35 (no checkout error series was returned for the 10:17:35-11:05:00 baseline), located on its client call oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct (292.3) and oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (292.3).

frontend-proxy error spans rose from 7.15 in the 10:17:35-11:05:00 baseline to 7243.9 in 11:05:00-11:17:35, and over the last hour they are on span_name ingress (3473.3) and router frontend egress (3460.1), i.e. on the path that fronts frontend traffic.

Among the 21 Deployments in otel-demo, only product-catalog has an overridden, non-runnable command (["invalid-command"]); the only other command/args overrides are flagd's legitimate ["/flagd-build","start",...] and otel-collector's args ['--config=/conf/relay.yaml'], and frontend's own container has no command override.

cart, currency, shipping, payment, accounting and fraud-detection show no error-span increase in 11:05:00-11:17:35 (payment, accounting and fraud-detection are exactly 0; cart, currency and shipping returned no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series at all), and ad's error count was effectively unchanged (1.03 in the 47-minute baseline versus 1.07 in the incident window), so these are background or unaffected rather than part of this failure path.

fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-8bpr4 changed during the authorized window for a different reason: its container last terminated with exitCode 137 reason OOMKilled finishedAt 2026-11-17T10:56:15Z, it restarted (restartCount 1) and is now running and ready, and fraud-detection has 0 error spans in both the baseline and incident windows.

Hypothesis that the flagd feature flag productCatalogFailure caused the frontend errors is rejected: flagd-config's demo.flagd.json sets productCatalogFailure defaultVariant to "off", and the product-catalog failure is a container-start failure (exec "invalid-command" not found, exitCode 128) rather than an application-level per-product error; product-catalog also emitted no STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans, only STATUS_CODE_UNSET ones.

Hypothesis that the fraud-detection OOMKill (10:56:15Z) contributed to the frontend error rate is rejected: the pod restarted and is ready, fraud-detection has zero error spans in both windows, and checkout's failing calls in the incident window target ProductCatalogService/GetProduct rather than fraud-detection.

The causal mechanism, supported by correlation and by the empty ready-endpoint set, is that the removal of all ready product-catalog endpoints after the 11:06:21Z pod deletion made frontend's outbound grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct calls (and recommendation's ListProducts and checkout's GetProduct calls) fail, which surfaced as frontend's error-span rate; the individual span error messages cannot be confirmed because Jaeger holds no traces for the incident window.

Restore the product-catalog Deployment pod template to the image's default entrypoint (remove container command ["invalid-command"]), then verify: a new ReplicaSet rolls out, pod product-catalog-fcf7564cf-* becomes Ready with 0 restarts, Service product-catalog gains a ready address, product-catalog span rate returns to its pre-11:06 level, and frontend/recommendation/checkout/frontend-proxy error spans return to baseline.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alerting rule is not present in this Prometheus: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate and with type=alert both returned nothing, so the alert's exact PromQL, its window and the reported 'current: 16.8666' could not be verified; the closest frontend error readings I could compute at 11:08:03Z were 1.72 errors/s over 5m and 5.17 errors/s over 2m, which do not reproduce 16.87.

http_server_request_duration_seconds_count and rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count{service_name="frontend"} returned no series in this Prometheus, so any HTTP- or RPC-label-based error-rate metric behind the alert is unknown rather than zero.

Jaeger's newest returned data ends at about 2026-11-17T10:51:30Z, so no incident-window trace could be read; the exact gRPC status codes and error messages of the failing frontend/recommendation/checkout calls to product-catalog remain unknown.

The actor or tooling that changed the product-catalog Deployment pod template (generation 4, new ReplicaSet product-catalog-fcf7564cf at 11:06:12Z) could not be identified; the change_history integration is not available in this Run.
frontend container logs returned zero lines (current stream status read, 0 bytes), so frontend's own application log evidence for these errors could not be inspected.

One-minute-range increase readings for frontend error spans returned 0 across 11:01-11:15 while the raw counter rose from 2045 to 15534 and 5-minute increases were large; those 1m readings are internally inconsistent and were not used as evidence.

Cluster object state and events were read after the window; the product-catalog Deployment's earlier template revisions (generations 1-3) and the reason the ReplicaSet product-catalog-fcf7564cf was briefly scaled to 0 at 11:06:21Z are not observable.
next_steps: Revert the product-catalog Deployment container command to the image default and confirm a ready endpoint plus restored product-catalog span rate.
Use cluster audit/change history (not integrated here) to identify who or what set command ["invalid-command"] on Deployment product-catalog shortly before 11:06:12Z.
Reconcile the RequestErrorRate alert definition with the available metrics; add or restore the http/rpc error metrics it expects so the reported 16.87 value can be traced to a series.
After recovery, confirm frontend, recommendation, checkout and frontend-proxy error spans return to their pre-11:06 baseline.
Investigate the separate fraud-detection OOMKill (exitCode 137 at 10:56:15Z) and its memory limit as an unrelated reliability issue.
